title: Ice Emoji 🧊 Meaning: Cold, Diamonds and “Ice Cold”
description: The 🧊 ice emoji means ice cubes and cold drinks, but also diamonds, a cold-hearted attitude, clutch performances and, in US politics, the agency ICE.
summary: The 🧊 ice emoji shows an ice cube. It means cold drinks and freezing temperatures, and in slang it stands for diamonds and jewelry, for being cold-hearted or unbothered, and for staying calm under pressure. In American political posts it is also shorthand for the immigration agency ICE.
meaning: At the literal level 🧊 is about cold things: iced coffee, cocktails, coolers, ice baths, a freezing morning. Added in 2019, it gave people a way to specify “iced” in a drink order or to complain about the weather without resorting to a snowflake. Athletes use it for recovery, as in icing a knee, and wellness fans use it for cold plunges and ice rollers.

Slang built on it quickly. In hip-hop, “ice” has long meant diamonds, so 🧊 on a photo of a watch or chain means the jewelry is impressive, and “iced out” means covered in it. As a description of character, ice is coldness: a brutal reply or a person who shows no emotion is “ice cold” or simply 🧊. This can be an insult, for heartlessness, or admiration, for someone unbothered who gives nothing away.

Sports gave it another positive sense. A player with “ice in their veins” makes the decisive shot without nerves, and fans post 🧊 or 🥶 after a clutch moment. In a different arena entirely, the letters ICE are the abbreviation for US Immigration and Customs Enforcement, and the emoji is used in posts about the agency, often as a warning that agents have been seen in an area or as a way to mention it without typing the name.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: Daily use is practical or teasing. It specifies an iced drink, reports the weather, or reminds someone to buy a bag for the party. As a reaction, 🧊 calls a message cold, as when a friend delivers a savage one-liner. It can also describe being left on read: “he's been 🧊 all week.”

contexts.label: In sports
contexts.body: Clutch plays earn it. A late free throw, a penalty kick under pressure or a game-winning putt is “ice,” and the athlete is praised with 🧊 in replies. Hockey fans use it more literally for the rink. It also appears in injury updates, where a player is icing a sprain.

contexts.label: On TikTok and Instagram
contexts.body: Jewelry and fashion posts use it to show off diamonds. Skincare creators use it for facial icing and cold therapy. “Cold” outfit photos, meaning stylish ones, pick it up alongside 🥶. Iced drink recipes and oddly satisfying ice-restocking videos give it a steady literal presence too.

contexts.label: In politics and news
contexts.body: In the United States, 🧊 commonly refers to Immigration and Customs Enforcement. Community alerts, protest posts and commentary use it for sightings of agents or criticism of the agency. People on various sides of the immigration debate recognize the shorthand. In such threads it has nothing to do with temperature.

examples.text: She replied “k” to his whole paragraph 🧊
examples.meaning: Commenting that a response was cold and dismissive.

examples.text: Down two, three seconds left, and he drains it. 🧊 in his veins
examples.meaning: Praising an athlete's composure under pressure.

examples.text: 🧊 spotted near the bus station, stay alert
examples.meaning: A community warning that immigration agents are in the area.

combos.meaning: Extremely cold weather, or a very stylish or clutch moment.
Ice in the veins; nerveless under pressure.

confusedWith.difference: ❄️ stands for snow, winter and cold weather, and as an insult for someone easily offended. 🧊 is solid ice: drinks, diamonds and cold attitudes.
🥶 is a frozen blue face that shows how a person feels, either freezing or impressed by something “cold.” 🧊 names the quality itself and is not a facial expression.
💎 is a literal diamond, used for jewelry, value and “diamond hands.” 🧊 refers to diamonds only through slang and has a cooler, more hip-hop inflection.

avoid: Don't post it as a joke in threads about immigration enforcement, where it may be taken as a real alert or a political statement.
Avoid calling a grieving or withdrawn person 🧊; what looks like coldness may be distress.
design: Vendors depict clear or pale blue ice with visible facets and highlights. Depending on the platform, the emoji shows a single translucent cube or a small pile of them, sometimes with a slight melt at the base. The color stays in the icy blue-white range everywhere, which also helps it suggest diamonds.

faqs.a: It has three main slang senses: diamonds or flashy jewelry, a cold and emotionless attitude, and calm under pressure, from the phrase “ice in the veins.” The topic of the conversation tells you which one applies.

faqs.q: What does 🧊 mean from a guy or girl?
faqs.a: It might mean they think something was cold, either harsh or impressively cool. It could describe someone giving the cold shoulder. Or it is literal: a drink or the weather. It is not a flirtatious emoji.

faqs.q: Why do people use 🧊 for immigration?
faqs.a: ICE is the abbreviation for US Immigration and Customs Enforcement. The emoji is a quick visual substitute for the acronym, used in alerts and political discussion, and sometimes chosen in the belief that it is less likely to be filtered.

Together they intensify “cold.” Depending on context that means freezing weather, a ruthless comment, a great outfit, or a clutch sports play. In all the slang cases it is praise for something done with icy confidence.

faqs.q: When was the ice emoji added?
faqs.a: It was introduced in 2019 as part of Emoji 12.0. Before then people used the snowflake or the cold face to convey the same ideas.
